checks.label: Add or subtract the percentage from 100% and find this percentage of the amount: up 20% is 120% of £150 = £180, up 15% is 115% of 40 A = 46 A, down 15% is 85% of £80 = £68, down 20% is 80% of £60 = £48, up 150% is 250% of 30 m = 75 m, down 4% is 96% of 230 V = 220.8 V, and each multiplier is that percentage ÷ 100
The multiplier does in one step what the two steps do, finding the change and adding it or taking it away: 150 + 30 = 180, 80 − 12 = 68, 230 − 9.2 = 220.8, 80 + 6 = 86, and so on every screen

A single multiplier does a cut too: a cut's multiplier is under 1 (× 0.85, × 0.8, × 0.75, × 0.96, × 0.92) and a rise's is over 1 (× 1.2, × 1.15, × 1.03, × 2, × 2.5, × 1.075), so a rise stretches the amount and a cut squeezes it

Dividing by 10 and not 100 reads 3% as 0.3, so a 3% rise gets a multiplier of 1.3; dividing by 100 gives 120% a multiplier of 1.2 and up 3% a multiplier of 1.03, and the 3% puzzle offers × 1.3 as that slip

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and every wrong answer offered is the one a named slip gives: adding the percentage as a number, stopping at the change on its own, dividing by 10 instead of 100, or using a rise's multiplier for a cut

The drag puzzle takes £90 only with the end on 75%, what is left after 25% off; with the end not yet moved the hint says drag it first, on 25% it names the part taken off, above 75% it says drag left, below it right; the end snaps to 5% steps from 0 to 100%

The bar stretches and squeezes by the multiplier: on every screen, finished, the new amount's bracket is the old one's length times the multiplier, the shading ends where it does, and its label pairs that percentage with the amount the working gives (150 × 1.2 = £180)
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows the new amount, the change or the multiplier

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart, each once the travel before it has ended

Nothing counts too fast or resizes: on every demonstration the new amount (and on step 5 the working) changes at most every 0.2 s while the end travels, in steps of 5% (25% for up 100%), its pill never changing width; after a right answer the tag shows only the final amount
